title: A linear-algebraic formulation of dimensional analysis with constraints
summary: Dimensional analysis, especially Buckingham's $π$ theorem, reduces the number of variables by rewriting a relation in terms of dimensionless quantities. When variables are tied by definitions, constitutive laws, or other constraints, however, eliminating variables in advance can be awkward. We formulate dimensional analysis with constraints as linear algebra in logarithmic variables.
